data.name: Main_SectionUsages
data.value: WHAT YOU CAN DO WITH IT

data.name: Main_Disclaimer
data.value: Guidelines based on EC Regulation No 589/2008 and ANSES recommendations. If in doubt about the look or smell of an egg, throw it away.

data.name: Code_Savoir1
data.value: The shell code does not indicate the laying date: it only identifies the farming method, country and farm.

data.name: Code_Savoir2
data.value: To check freshness, use the date printed on the box (the best-before date) in the Freshness tab. The laying date is 28 days before that date.

data.name: Code_Savoir3
data.value: First digit: 0 for organic, 1 for free range, 2 for barn-raised, 3 for caged.

data.name: Code_ScanIllisible
data.value: Code unreadable. Move closer, position the egg flat and facing the camera, and avoid cast shadows.

data.name: Code_ScanRelire
data.value: Double-check the code before validating: on a shell, 0/O, 1/I and 5/S are easily confused.

data.name: Conseils_Dcr1
data.value: The date printed on the box is a recommended-consumption date, set at 28 days after laying. It is not a use-by date.

data.name: Conseils_Dcr2
data.value: Past this date, an egg with an intact shell kept refrigerated remains edible for a few more weeks, provided it is cooked thoroughly. At the slightest doubt — smell, cloudy white, cracked shell — throw it away.

data.name: Conseils_Dcr3
data.value: Sale to consumers, however, is banned beyond 21 days after laying, i.e. one week before the best-before date.

data.name: Conseils_Disclaimer
data.value: Sources: EC Regulation No 589/2008 and ANSES recommendations. This app provides guidelines, it does not replace your own judgement.

data.name: Egg_Resume_Future
data.value: The date you entered is in the future. Check the laying date or the best-before date on the box.

data.name: Egg_Resume_ExtraFrais
data.value: Laid {0} ago. Every use is possible, including raw or lightly cooked. {1} days left before the best-before date.

data.name: Egg_Resume_Frais
data.value: Laid {0} days ago. Still within its recommended consumption period {1}, but preferably eaten well cooked.

data.name: Egg_Resume_ApresDcr
data.value: Laid {0} days ago, {1} past the best-before date. Best-before is not a use-by date: if the shell is intact and the egg was kept refrigerated, it is still edible, but only cooked thoroughly. Do the water glass test first.

data.name: Egg_Resume_Douteux
data.value: Laid {0} days ago. Too old: better to throw it away, even if it looks normal.

data.name: Egg_Conseil_EF_Cru_Detail
data.value: Reserved for extra-fresh eggs. Prepare at the last moment, keep refrigerated and eat within 24 hours. Avoid for children, pregnant women, the elderly or immunocompromised people.

data.name: Egg_Conseil_EF_Coque_Detail
data.value: This is the ideal moment: the white is firm and holds together well.

data.name: Egg_Conseil_EF_Dur_Detail
data.value: Possible, but a very fresh egg peels poorly. Wait 7 to 10 days for easy peeling.

data.name: Egg_Conseil_F_Cru_Detail
data.value: Not recommended beyond 9 days after laying. Prefer an extra-fresh egg.

data.name: Egg_Conseil_F_Coque_Detail
data.value: Lightly cooked: to avoid. The yolk does not reach a sufficient temperature.

data.name: Egg_Conseil_F_Plat_Detail
data.value: Yes, cooking the white and yolk thoroughly.

data.name: Egg_Conseil_F_Dur_Detail
data.value: Ideal use at this stage, and it peels easily.

data.name: Egg_Conseil_AD_Cru_Detail
data.value: Excluded. No raw, soft-boiled, medium-boiled or poached preparation.

data.name: Egg_Conseil_AD_Dur_Detail
data.value: Possible if the water glass test is conclusive. Cook 10 min from boiling point.

data.name: Egg_Conseil_AD_Cuisson_Usage
data.value: Cooked through (cake, quiche, gratin, well-cooked omelette)

data.name: Egg_Conseil_AD_Cuisson_Detail
data.value: The white and yolk must be fully set. Aim for 70 °C (158 °F) at the core.

data.name: Egg_Conseil_AD_Odeur_Detail
data.value: Crack the egg into a separate bowl: the slightest sulphurous smell or a cloudy, runny white means throw it away.

data.name: Egg_Conseil_D_Tous_Detail
data.value: Beyond about six weeks after laying, the risk isn't worth the saving. Throw the egg away.

data.name: Egg_Conseil_D_NeCassez_Usage
data.value: Don't crack it over a dish

data.name: Egg_Conseil_D_NeCassez_Detail
data.value: A spoiled egg can contaminate an entire dish.

data.name: Egg_Conservation_1
data.value: Never wash eggs: it destroys the shell's protective cuticle.

data.name: Egg_Conservation_2
data.value: Keep them at a constant temperature. An egg taken from the cold then warmed up gets covered in condensation, which helps bacteria get through.

data.name: Egg_Conservation_3
data.value: In the fridge, place them on a shelf rather than in the door, where the temperature fluctuates.

data.name: Egg_Conservation_4
data.value: Store them pointed end down, away from strong-smelling food: the shell is porous.

data.name: Egg_Conservation_5
data.value: Once hard-boiled and peeled, eat them within 2 to 3 days.

data.name: Egg_TestVerre_1
data.value: Fill a glass with cold water and drop the egg in.

data.name: Egg_TestVerre_2
data.value: It stays lying on the bottom: very fresh, no concern.

data.name: Egg_TestVerre_3
data.value: It stands upright on the bottom: still edible, but cook it well.

data.name: Egg_TestVerre_4
data.value: It floats: the air pocket is too big, throw it away without opening it.

data.name: ShellCode_Mode_Cage_Detail
